chapter: Sarah Vaughan and the Basie band
title: John Collins's promise and choosing family over fame
summary: Chicago and New York musicians thought Collins would break through, but he chose to raise his daughters.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Back to Chicago. Did John get a great deal of recognition, or just from the musicians who heard him? I mean was he recognized when he was young as having great promise?
Did he make something of a name for himself there?
Yeah. Well, now, let's see, between

Chicago and New York we thought that John was the next one to break through. You had your Charlie Christiansen, and -- who else? But we just knew that John Collins was a man that could break through. But as I mentioned before, he became a family man. And you have to sacrifice -- it's a very lucky man that can do both.

Because the situations just don't allow that, you know. And he had to -- he wanted to grow up with his daughters, you know. But he was just the man that we thought was going to -- you know, we knew what he could do.
